Payroll rates, wage bases and limits for employers in 2027
As of November 18, 2026, the Social Security wage base ($192,300), the 401(k) deferral limit ($25,500), the health FSA limit ($3,500) and the HSA limits ($4,500 self-only, $9,000 family) are published for 2027, and the Department of Labor’s final 2026 FUTA credit reduction list names California at 1.5 percent. The IRS has not announced 2027 standard mileage rates, and no IRS page read on that date states a 2027 dependent care limit.

Revenue Procedures 2026-22, 2026-24 and 2026-26 print no date, so the table shows the Internal Revenue Bulletin issue date for each.
What is the Social Security wage base for 2027?
The Social Security Administration states that the contribution and benefit base for earnings in 2027 is $192,300, up from $184,500 for 2026. The SSA contribution and benefit base page states the 2027 figure, and the 2027 fact sheet lists both years and is linked from the SSA’s October 14, 2026 press release. The base applies to Social Security tax only. The SSA prints $11,922.60 as the Social Security contribution for an individual with wages at or above $192,300, and the same amount for the employer.
Do Social Security and Medicare tax rates change in 2027?
The Social Security tax rate for wages paid in 2027 is set by statute at 6.2 percent for employees and employers each, the Medicare rate is 1.45 percent each on all wages, and the SSA’s 2027 fact sheet shows the combined employee rate unchanged at 7.65 percent. The SSA contribution and benefit base page states the statutory rates, and the 2027 fact sheet states that the 7.65 percent combined rate does not include the 0.9 percent Additional Medicare Tax.
When does Additional Medicare Tax withholding start?
An employer withholds the 0.9 percent Additional Medicare Tax on wages paid to an employee above $200,000 in a calendar year, beginning in the pay period in which wages exceed $200,000, under Publication 15 (2026). The publication states that the tax is imposed only on the employee and that there is no employer share. As of November 18, 2026, no final 2027 IRS publication states this withholding threshold, so the rule comes from Publication 15 (2026).
What is the 401(k) deferral limit for 2027?
In Notice 2026-66, announced on November 12, 2026, the IRS raised the 2027 limit on elective deferrals to 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457 plans and the Thrift Savings Plan to $25,500, up from $24,500 for 2026. The IRS announced the notice in news release IR-2026-136. SIMPLE plans and starter 401(k) plans have their own limits.
What are the 2027 catch-up limits for employees age 50 and over and ages 60 to 63?
Notice 2026-66 sets the 2027 catch-up limit in plans other than SIMPLE plans at $8,500 for employees age 50 and over, up from $8,000, and at $11,750 instead of $8,500 for individuals who attain age 60, 61, 62 or 63 in 2027, up from $11,250 for 2026. IR-2026-136 states that participants age 50 and older generally can contribute up to $34,000 each year starting in 2027 in most 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457 plans and the Thrift Savings Plan.
What Roth catch-up wage threshold does the IRS state in Notice 2026-66?
Notice 2026-66 states that the Roth catch-up wage threshold for 2026, which section 414(v)(7)(A) uses to decide whether an individual’s catch-up contributions to an applicable employer plan (other than a plan described in section 408(k) or (p)) for 2027 must be designated as Roth contributions, is increased from $150,000 to $155,000.
What are the 2027 SIMPLE and IRA limits?
Notice 2026-66 sets the 2027 SIMPLE plan general salary reduction limit at $17,500, up from $17,000, and states that the IRA contribution limit remains $7,500. The notice also states these amounts.


* A SIMPLE limit of $19,100 for certain eligible employers, up from $18,100.
* A SIMPLE catch-up limit that remains $4,000 for age 50 and over and remains $5,250 for individuals who attain age 60, 61, 62 or 63 in 2027.
* An IRA catch-up limit for age 50 and over that remains $1,100.
Which 2027 plan limits affect plan testing and design?
Notice 2026-66 sets the 2027 defined contribution plan limit at $75,000 (up from $72,000), the annual compensation limit at $375,000 (up from $360,000), the highly compensated employee threshold at $170,000 (up from $160,000) and the key employee threshold for top-heavy plans at $245,000 (up from $235,000). The notice also states these amounts.


* A defined benefit annual benefit limit of $300,000, up from $290,000, effective January 1, 2027.
* A starter 401(k) and safe harbor deferral-only plan limit of $6,500, up from $6,000, increased by $1,100 for individuals who attain age 50 before the end of the taxable year.
* A SEP compensation threshold that remains $800.
What are the 2027 health FSA limit and carryover amount?
Revenue Procedure 2026-35 sets the health flexible spending arrangement salary reduction limit for taxable years beginning in 2027 at $3,500, and IRS news release IR-2026-133 describes that as up $100 from the prior year. If the cafeteria plan permits carryover of unused amounts, the maximum carryover amount is $700, which the release describes as an increase of $20. The IRS announced both amounts on November 5, 2026.
What are the 2027 HSA contribution limits and high deductible health plan minimums?
Revenue Procedure 2026-24 sets the 2027 HSA contribution limit at $4,500 for self-only coverage and $9,000 for family coverage. For 2027, the revenue procedure defines a high deductible health plan as one with an annual deductible of not less than $1,750 for self-only coverage or $3,500 for family coverage and annual out-of-pocket expenses, which include deductibles and co-payments but not premiums, of not more than $8,700 for self-only coverage or $17,400 for family coverage. For comparison, the IRS Publication 969 page states 2026 limits of $4,400 for self-only coverage and $8,750 for family coverage.
Has the IRS published a 2027 dependent care FSA limit?
As of November 18, 2026, the IRS has not announced 2027 standard mileage rates, and no IRS page read on that date states a 2027 dependent care assistance limit. Publication 15-B (2026) states that for the 2026 tax year the annual dependent care FSA limit was raised from $5,000 to $7,500 ($2,500 to $3,750 for married filing separately). Revenue Procedure 2026-35, which sets the 2027 health FSA and transportation amounts, has no dependent care item.
What are the 2027 monthly transit and parking limits?
Revenue Procedure 2026-35 sets the qualified transportation fringe limit for taxable years beginning in 2027 at $350 per month for the aggregate of transportation in a commuter highway vehicle and any transit pass, and at $350 per month for qualified parking. IRS news release IR-2026-133 describes the amount as up $10 from 2026.
What are the 2027 ACA employer shared responsibility amounts and required contribution percentage?
For 2027, Revenue Procedure 2026-22 states the indexed per-employee annual dollar amounts used to calculate employer shared responsibility payments, $3,780 (the adjusted $2,000 amount under section 4980H(c)(1)) and $5,670 (the adjusted $3,000 amount under section 4980H(b)(1)), and Revenue Procedure 2026-26 states a required contribution percentage of 10.22 percent under section 36B for plan years beginning in 2027. Revenue Procedure 2026-22 applies to taxable years and plan years beginning after December 31, 2026. The IRS employer shared responsibility page says each payment is calculated on a monthly basis and is not a flat amount for all applicable large employer members. Revenue Procedure 2026-26 states that the 10.22 percent is used under section 36B to determine whether an individual is eligible for affordable employer-sponsored minimum essential coverage.
What is the Form 1099 reporting threshold for payments made in 2027?
Revenue Procedure 2026-35 states that for payments made in calendar year 2027 the reporting threshold for payments described in section 6041(a) is $2,100. The IRS announced the revenue procedure on November 5, 2026. For returns required to be filed in 2028 and statements required to be furnished in 2028, the same revenue procedure states a general penalty of $360 per return or statement.
What are the FUTA rate and wage base, and do they change for 2027?
Publication 15 (2026) states that the 2026 FUTA tax rate is 6.0 percent on the first $7,000 paid to each employee as wages during the year, and as of November 18, 2026 no final IRS publication states a FUTA rate or wage base for 2027. The publication says the credit may be as much as 5.4 percent of FUTA taxable wages, which brings the rate to 0.6 percent when the employer paid state unemployment taxes in full, on time and on the same wages and the state is not a credit reduction state.
Has the FUTA credit reduction list for 2026 been published?
The Department of Labor has published the final 2026 FUTA credit reductions on its FUTA credit reduction page, updated November 12, 2026. California employers are subject to a 1.5 percent credit reduction, and the U.S. Virgin Islands repaid its advances before November 10, 2026 and has no reduction. The Department of Labor says employers in a credit reduction state incur a FUTA tax rate of 0.6 percent plus the FUTA credit reduction. Publication 15 (2026) says employers include the credit reduction liability with the fourth quarter deposit, and the added amount is not due until the due date for that deposit.
Which states have published their 2027 unemployment taxable wage bases?
As of November 18, 2026, the agency pages for Washington, California, Colorado, Utah, Oregon, New Jersey and Nevada state a 2027 unemployment taxable wage base.


* Washington employers pay unemployment payroll taxes on the first $82,000 paid to each employee beginning in 2027, up from $78,200 in 2026, according to the Employment Security Department release of June 10, 2026.
* California says the 2027 unemployment insurance taxable wage limit is $7,000 per employee per calendar year, and the Employment Training Tax rate is 0.1 percent on a $7,000 wage limit, on its rates and withholding page.
* Colorado says the 2027 chargeable wage base increased to $32,100 from $30,600 in 2026 and that the 2027 solvency surcharge is not in effect, on its premium rates page.
* Utah says the 2027 taxable wage base is $52,700 and that wages above it are reported but not taxed, on its tax rates page.
* Oregon says the 2027 unemployment insurance taxable wage base is $58,600 per employee and that it mailed 2027 individual employer rate information by November 13, 2026 and posted it to employer online accounts on November 15, 2026, on its current tax rate page.
* New Jersey says the 2027 taxable wage base is $46,400 for unemployment insurance, the Workforce Development and Supplemental Workforce Funds (workers and employers) and temporary disability insurance (employers), and $177,100 for temporary disability insurance and family leave insurance (workers only), on its rate information page.
* Nevada says the taxable wage base for calendar year 2027 is $45,400, compared with $43,700 for 2026, on its unemployment insurance tax page.


This list does not state a 2027 base for any other state, including Idaho, Minnesota, Alaska and Wyoming, so employers in other states should confirm the figure with their state workforce agency.
Which state paid family and medical leave rates for 2027 are already published?
As of November 18, 2026, state agency pages for Washington, California, New York, Colorado, Minnesota, New Jersey, Maryland, Massachusetts and Oregon state 2027 paid leave or disability insurance rates or contribution amounts.


* Washington says the Paid Family and Medical Leave premium rate is 1.2 percent of an employee’s gross wages starting January 1, 2027, compared with 1.13 percent in 2026, with employers paying at least 29.3 percent of the total premium and employees at most 70.7 percent. The page says businesses classified as having fewer than 50 employees are not required to pay the employer portion but must still collect or pay the employee premium, and first-quarter 2027 premiums and reports are due by the end of April 2027.
* California says the State Disability Insurance withholding rate for 2027 is 1.4 percent, compared with 1.3 percent in 2026, and that all wages are subject to SDI contributions.
* New York says employees will contribute 0.452 percent of their gross wages per pay period to Paid Family Leave in 2027, with a maximum annual contribution of $451.81.
* Colorado says the 2027 FAMLI premium rate will be 0.86 percent of wages, down from 0.88 percent in 2026, effective January 1, 2027, for employers using a FAMLI plan, in a bulletin sent September 30, 2026.
* Minnesota says the Paid Leave premium rate is 0.88 percent for 2026 and 2027, made up of 0.27 percent for family leave and 0.61 percent for medical leave, with a 0.66 percent small employer rate for employers with 30 or fewer workers in each quarter and an average wage of no more than 150 percent of the statewide average wage. Employers can collect up to 0.44 percent from employees or choose to cover more, and premiums are capped at the Social Security wage limit.
* New Jersey prints worker contribution rates for January 1 to December 31, 2027 of 0.0024 for disability insurance and 0.0024 for family leave insurance, which are 0.24 percent each.
* Maryland says the initial FAMLI contribution rate is 0.9 percent of wages up to the Social Security wage cap for wages paid January 1 through December 31, 2027, split equally between employers and employees at 0.45 percent each, and employers can withhold up to 50 percent of the rate. Employers with fewer than 15 total employees, counting Maryland and out-of-state employees, remit only 50 percent of the rate, and the first payment, for wages paid January 1 to March 31, 2027, is due April 30, 2027.
* Massachusetts says Chapter 101 of the Acts of 2026 shifts employer contributions from medical leave to family leave effective January 1, 2027, with contributions capped by the Social Security taxable maximum. For employers with 25 or more covered individuals, the 2027 family leave contribution allows up to 40 percent to be withheld from the covered individual (0.28 percent of eligible wages) with the employer contributing the remaining 60 percent (0.42 percent), and up to 100 percent of the medical leave contribution (0.18 percent of eligible wages) can be withheld. For employers with fewer than 25 covered individuals, the effective contribution rate is 0.46 percent of eligible wages, with the employer share of the family leave contribution not required.
* Oregon says the 2027 Paid Leave contribution rate is 1 percent of subject wages up to $192,300 per employee.


This list does not state 2027 rates for any other state or program, so employers elsewhere should confirm rates with the state agency.
Has the IRS announced the 2027 standard mileage rate?
As of November 18, 2026, the IRS has not announced 2027 standard mileage rates, and its standard mileage rates page lists no 2027 rate. The page lists the 2026 business rate as 72.5 cents per mile for January 1 to June 30, 2026 and 76 cents per mile for July 1 to December 31, 2026.
Which 2027 figures are still not published, and can I rely on IRS draft forms?
As of November 18, 2026, the primary pages read on that date state no 2027 standard mileage rate, no 2027 dependent care FSA limit, no final 2027 FUTA rate or wage base, no final 2027 federal income tax withholding tables, and no final 2026 Form 940 instructions or Schedule A. The IRS has posted only early release drafts of those 2026 Form 940 materials, of Publication 15 for 2027 and of Form 941 (Rev. March 2027). The IRS labels its early release drafts of 2027 forms and publications “not for filing” and says not to rely on draft instructions or publications. For a figure that is not yet published, check the issuing agency again before relying on it.
